summary: Burst reservation failover triggers degraded P99 throughput and imbalanced batching for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleDocs) reports a sudden spike in P99 token latency and a ~35% drop in measured throughput for their dedicated pool after an automated burst-reservation failover event. Impact: multiple application endpoints experienced increased tail latency leading to user-facing timeouts.

Impact:
- ~35% drop in throughput for tenant-specific routes starting 2026-03-12T17:12:00Z.
- P99 token latency increased from ~180ms to ~820ms for short chat requests (<= 128 tokens).
- Errors increased: transient 504s and client-observed timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: pool-id dp-45-nimble
- Region: us-west-2 (customer dedicated nodes)
- Runtime: 1.8.3 (serving runtime)
- Autoscaler: predictive-autoscale v2.1

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler triggered a burst capacity failover at 17:11:42Z when reserved node set hit soft-capacity and a scheduled burst was rejected by quota check.
- Scheduler started evacuations of several tenant slots; eviction logs show KV cache drop and checkpoint flushes.
- Following evictions, request batching became imbalanced: many small batches (1-2 requests) processed on fallback low-throughput instances while few large batches queued behind OOM-guard checks.
- GPU utilization on surviving nodes dropped to ~45% while queue length and wait time increased, indicating underutilized GPUs but scheduling bottlenecks.

Expected behavior:
- When burst-reservation fails, traffic should be routed to compatible dedicated variants without causing widespread eviction/imbalanced batching or tail-latency regressions.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends high-concurrency short-chat traffic (200 RPS, avg 80 tokens) to tenant pool until soft-reservation threshold is reached.
2) Force quota rejection for burst-reservation (simulate reduced burst quota via control-plane toggle).
3) Observe autoscaler decisions and eviction logs in cluster dp-45-nimble around failover time.
4) Note p99 latency and batching histogram in Console -> per-route metrics.
logs: 2026-03-12T17:11:41Z scheduler: eviction initiated for slot t-912 (reason: burst-failover)
2026-03-12T17:11:43Z serving-runtime: kv-cache flush start tenant=t-912 size=1.2GB
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler failed to place new burst nodes and eviction strategy triggered wide slot shuffling which polluted KV caches across nodes.
Console traces show a spike in KV cache misses and increased mem-copy times after eviction events — suggests cold caches caused repeated recomputation/rehydration costs.
GPU utilization low on nodes that accepted traffic after failover; suggests throughput constrained by scheduler/worker startup and caching rather than raw GPU compute.
Confirmed autoscaler logged 'quota_exceeded' for burst pool at 17:11:42Z. Quota check path returned HTTP 403 from control-plane while capacity signals indicated pending work.
Related patterns differ from usual noisy-neighbor GPU hogging: here GPUs are idle but serving latency is high due to imbalanced batching and KV cache churn.

Cross-referenced similar symptom cluster SUP-20168 and SUP-51777 for eviction and intermittent GPU availability; however root cause here ties to burst reservation gating logic and eviction policy timing.
comments: Support (Ava Martinez) 2026-03-12T18:05Z: Acknowledged. Opening incident. Collected initial logs and asked customer to lower concurrency as temporary mitigation.

SRE (Marcus Chen) 2026-03-12T18:40Z: Confirmed quota_exceeded event from control-plane. Requesting control-plane team to validate burst quota service between 17:10-17:13Z. Also triggered deeper heap traces on one affected runtime node.
Customer (NimbleDocs - Elena Park) 2026-03-12T19:02Z: We hit the regressions during a product demo. Lowering concurrency to 50 RPS helped but not ideal. Please advise next steps.
Control-plane (Rohit Desai) 2026-03-12T20:15Z: Burst quota service returned 403 due to a transient cache invalidation — rolling a hotfix to reduce false negatives. Will post PR link.
SRE (Marcus Chen) 2026-03-13T09:12Z: Deployed autoscaler guard in canary that prefers in-pool spillover before eviction. Running soak; initial telemetry shows reduced eviction churn.

Support (Ava Martinez) 2026-03-14T08:22Z: Customer approved temporary traffic shaping and pinning to smaller quantized model; reporting P99 has returned to ~220ms and throughput recovered to ~90% of baseline.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer traffic temporarily routed to redwood/gpt-3-8b-int8 and tenant rate-limited to 60 RPS while autoscaler hotfix rolled. Control-plane fix to burst quota validation deployed and autoscaler eviction policy adjusted to reduce cross-slot cache invalidation. Post-action: implement fair-share batching policy in scheduler and add a soft-failover path that preserves KV caches when possible.
